scores.claim_text: ASTS has a federal contract with the U.S. Space Development Agency (SDA) — including a $43.0M contract via a prime contractor for testing services using the initial BB satellites, plus a direct $30.0M SDA Europa Track 2 commercial-solutions contract, plus an IDIQ award under the Missile Defense Agency's SHIELD program.
scores.M_check: usaspending.query_recipient_contracts (AST SPACEMOBILE, AST & Science, AST Space Mobile USA, AST LLC, SpaceMobile, AST Space; both all-agency and DoD-only). DoD-only AST SPACEMOBILE = 0 awards. Best canonical recipient hit = 'AST SPACE MOBILE USA LLC' with only 2 awards total: NASA $969,573 (legacy cubesat bus, ACS3 solar-sail, 2019-vintage award ID 80ARC019P0003) and DoD $500 SHIELD IDIQ stub (HQ085926FF777). No $30M direct SDA Europa Track 2 award visible; no $43M-equivalent obligation visible under the prime-contractor path.
scores.interpretation: Calibration Heuristic Layer 3 Rule 7 fires. The SHIELD IDIQ existence IS corroborated (a $500 'initial order' under HQ085926DG110 / HQ085926FF777 matches the 10-K's IDIQ disclosure), so the relationship is genuine. The $43M SDA-via-prime contract may legitimately be off-USAspending under ASTS's name because the obligation sits with the prime, so we cannot hard-refute that. HOWEVER the direct $30M SDA Europa Track 2 commercial-solutions contract SHOULD be visible in USAspending and is not — that is a partial contradiction. Net read: relationship-class verified (SHIELD IDIQ exists), but the headline dollar figures ($43M + $30M) are not corroborated at the dollar level on the most authoritative source. MODERATE: claim is stage-true but the dollar magnitudes are not yet observable, and the IDIQ has not produced any obligation beyond $500 as of pull date.

scores.claim_text: ASTS has definitive commercial agreements with AT&T (space-based wireless connectivity for the U.S.) and Verizon (definitive commercial agreement announced October 8, 2025 for direct-to-cellular service starting 2026), plus an existing AT&T agreement and strategic investments.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext: AT&T (CIK 0000732717) 'SpaceMobile' = 3 hits across 2023-07 8-K (Q2 2023 supplement), 2023-10 8-K (Q3 2023 supplement), 2025-04 DEF 14A. Verizon (CIK 0000732712) 'SpaceMobile' = 0 hits. External base rate (all filers) = 281 hits. Counterparty-disclosure threshold heuristic Rule 7 is partially asymmetric: AT&T has named ASTS in its own filings repeatedly (consistent with AT&T's strategic-investment and product narrative), while Verizon has not yet named SpaceMobile in any EDGAR-indexed filing through cutoff, despite ASTS claiming a definitive commercial agreement was 'announced October 8, 2025'.
scores.interpretation: AT&T arm: PASS. AT&T is the original strategic investor and has corroborated the partnership in its own 8-K supplements and proxy. Verizon arm: weaker — Verizon's filings through 2026-05-16 do not mention SpaceMobile at all. This is consistent with a recent (October 2025) commercial agreement that has not yet flowed into a 10-K/10-Q disclosure pattern at Verizon's materiality threshold — direct-to-cellular satellite services are an extension product, not yet a material revenue/cost line for VZ. Net: PASS — at least one of the two major US telco counterparties (AT&T) has unambiguously corroborated; the Verizon silence is consistent with stage (recent agreement, low materiality), not an active contradiction. Customer-pipeline claim is well-supported.

scores.claim_text: ASTS claims an intellectual-property portfolio of approximately 3,850 patent and patent-pending claims covering direct-to-cell satellite ecosystem (large phased array, beamforming, ASIC chip AST5000).
scores.M_check: uspto_odp.query_assignee under 'AST & Science' (LLC subsidiary holding the IP) returns 123 total applications and 55 granted patents pre-cutoff. Recent applications cover SATELLITE MIMO, CPRI satellite communication, LEO mechanical deployable structures, polarization-transparent channel switching in satellite-RAN, beam transition in satellite radio access network, and antenna calibration — all directly tied to the claimed tech (phased array, satellite, wireless cellular). Query under 'AST SpaceMobile' returns 0 (IP is held in the LLC subsidiary).

M_value.tech_alignment: phased_array + satellite RAN + LEO deployable structure + beam management — all directly on-thesis

scores.interpretation: Calibration Heuristic 8 PASS — n_granted (55) is well above the ≥10 threshold AND the granted/pending titles map directly to the company's claimed differentiating technology (large phased array, beamforming, satellite-RAN, deployable structures, satellite MIMO). The 3,850 'patent and patent-pending claims' figure refers to legal claim count across the portfolio (not patents); 123 applications × ~31 claims each is internally consistent. PASS.

scores.claim_text: ASTS has 5 Block 1 BB satellites in orbit (launched September 12, 2024) and launched its first Block 2 BB satellite (BB6) on December 23, 2025 — i.e. 6 commercial BB satellites in orbit at cutoff, with claimed near-term plans to initiate limited noncontinuous SpaceMobile service.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext: 'BlueBird' = 418 hits 2024-09 to cutoff; 'BlueWalker' = 71 hits 2022 to cutoff. External corroboration of the BlueBird launch narrative is substantial (high mention count across filings). The 10-K itself discloses (Item 1 + financial-statement notes) capitalization of exactly 5 Block 1 BB satellites in property-and-equipment 'satellites in orbit' AND a 6th (BB6, Block 2) launched 2025-12-23 with on-orbit phased-array deployment confirmed February 10, 2026.

M_value.commercial_service_status: not yet launched / zero service revenue

scores.interpretation: Calibration Heuristic 3 (planned vs operational) AND Heuristic 9 (constellation-operational vs constellation-announced) — the 6-satellites-in-orbit count is internally consistent and externally well-mentioned. HOWEVER the much larger constellation (multiple hundreds at design) required for global continuous SpaceMobile commercial service is NOT yet deployed. The 10-K explicitly states 'The SpaceMobile Service has not been launched and therefore has not yet generated any revenue.' Bright-line distinction (Heuristic 3): test-call demo + a handful of operational BBs is real; continuous commercial service is not. MODERATE — claim as stated is technically true but the marketing tier ('definitive commercial agreements / commercial service starting 2026') conflates demonstration capability with operational-network reality. Investors who interpret '6 BB satellites = commercial network online' would be misreading the stage.

scores.claim_text: ASTS operates satellite assembly, integration and test (AIT) facilities in Texas (Midland) headquartered there, plus engineering/production centers in Florida (Homestead), Maryland (Lanham), Spain, Israel, India, and Scotland — global footprint approximately 450,000 sq ft.
scores.M_check: epa_frs.query_facilities: 'AST SpaceMobile' in TX -> 1 facility — registry_id 110071516306, name 'AST SPACEMOBILE SITE 2', address 13600 W INTERSTATE 20, ODESSA TX (county Midland), zip 79765. FL, MD: 0 facilities (expected — engineering/office space typically below EPA reporting threshold).

M_value.county_match_to_10K: Midland (10-K says Midland, TX; EPA address sits in Odessa but FRS county field is Midland — these towns straddle the Midland-Ector county line in the Permian Basin)

scores.interpretation: Calibration Heuristic 1 PASS — propulsion/satellite-AIT facilities ARE EPA-regulated and the TX claim is confirmed in FRS at the right place. The 'Site 2' naming implies a Site 1 exists too. No FRS hits in FL or MD is consistent with those being engineering/office space (not chemical handling). 450,000 sq ft global footprint is not directly EPA-verifiable but the existence of the named Midland AIT facility is confirmed. PASS.

scores.claim_text: ASTS reports $2.8 billion of cash and restricted cash at 12/31/2025 (up from $567.5M at 12/31/2024), reported FY2025 net loss before NCI of approximately $461M; SpaceMobile Service has not been launched and has generated zero service revenue; risk factor explicitly references potential future going-concern qualifier. ASTS has a long history of heavily dilutive financings.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext (cik 0001780312): 'going concern' = 10 hits (consistent with persistent risk-factor language; no active GC qualifier flagged in the 10-K's audit opinion section). 'reverse stock split' = 9 hits (consistent with anti-takeover authorization language; no recent split executed). 'ATM' / at-the-market = 35 hits (extensive use of ATM equity-offering programs — classic dilutive financing pattern). 10-K self-reports: cash + restricted cash $2.8B at 12/31/2025 vs $567.5M at 12/31/2024 (i.e. ~$2.3B in net financing inflows over the year); FY2025 net loss before NCI of $461M; zero SpaceMobile service revenue.
scores.interpretation: Calibration Heuristic 10 (DELISTING / GOING-CONCERN) — the surface looks fine right now: $2.8B cash, no active going-concern qualifier, no recent reverse split. HOWEVER (a) the company has $0 service revenue and a $461M annual loss, with capex still required for the Block 2 production ramp, (b) the financing pattern (35 ATM-related mentions, repeated S-3 ATM filings, and the implied $2.23B 2025 net inflow) is classic 'dilution-funded R&D' — exactly the pattern Heuristic 10 warns about, (c) commentary in the 10-K explicitly preserves the future-going-concern flag. Net: NOT a current distress event, but the financing footprint IS persistent dilutive equity issuance and the next cash refresh round before commercial service ramps is essentially mandatory. MODERATE — claim as stated (current cash position) is accurately disclosed; the dilution-prone capital structure is corroborated and worth flagging.

scores.claim_text: Ten-year commercial agreement with Saudi Telecom Company (STC, October 29, 2025) for direct-to-device satellite mobile connectivity across Saudi Arabia and key regional markets; plus reseller agreement with jointly-owned European 'SatCo' Vodafone JV (December 18, 2025).
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext: Vodafone (CIK 0000839923) 'SpaceMobile' = 2 filings (20-F 2024-06 and 20-F 2025-06) — two consecutive Vodafone annual reports explicitly disclose the SpaceMobile relationship. SatCo = 18 hits across all filers (base rate); Saudi Telecom = 25 hits (base rate); STC = 468 (mostly non-SpaceMobile uses of STC as an acronym). Vodafone counterparty corroboration is strong; the SatCo JV is reflected in Vodafone's own 20-F disclosure pattern.
scores.interpretation: Calibration Heuristic 5 (source-jurisdiction) note: STC is a Saudi issuer — there is no EDGAR 20-F for STC, so we cannot directly verify the STC commercial agreement on US filings. However Vodafone IS a 20-F filer (CIK 839923) and has affirmed the SpaceMobile relationship in two consecutive annual reports including the most recent (2025-06), which post-dates ASTS's claim. The SatCo JV with Vodafone is corroborated by counterparty disclosure. PASS — the international-MNO partnership narrative is supported on at least one named counterparty's primary annual filing.

scores.claim_text: ASTS claims agreements with 'multiple launch vehicle providers' to secure launch contracts for the planned Block 2 BB constellation rollout. No specific named launch provider, vehicle name, or named launch site (Vandenberg/Cape Canaveral/Wallops) is given in Item 1.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext (cik 0001780312): 'launch services agreement' = 19 hits; 'SpaceX launch services' = 4 hits; 'Falcon 9' = 7 hits; 'ISRO' = 1 hit; 'Blue Origin launch services' = 0. So while Item 1 of the latest 10-K keeps providers anonymized as 'multiple launch vehicle providers', ASTS's full filing corpus has DISCLOSED actual launch counterparties (SpaceX/Falcon 9 explicitly named in 7+ filings, ISRO in 1).
scores.interpretation: Name-variant fragility (Heuristic 6) and counterparty-disclosure threshold (Heuristic 7) both satisfied. The launch-vehicle relationships are real, named in ASTS's own 8-Ks and S-3s (SpaceX/Falcon 9, ISRO/GSLV/PSLV implied). The 10-K's Item 1 generic 'multiple launch vehicle providers' phrasing is consistent with the company having signed master-services agreements that are individually disclosed in 8-K exhibits. PASS — claim is supported and Heuristic 11 (launch-cadence vs launch-manifest) is satisfied for the cadence achieved (Sep 2024 Block 1 batch + Dec 2025 Block 2 BB6).
